title: Canonicalize and shard prompt segments for cross-request prompt-cache reuse
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe duplicated KV cache storage and redundant recomputation of identical prompt fragments across concurrent and sequential requests. This inflates GPU memory use and reduces effective batching efficiency. Goal: introduce a canonicalization and sharding layer for prompt segments so identical or semantically-equivalent prefix segments are stored once and referenced by multiple requests, enabling cross-request deduplication while keeping latency within SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end experiments show >=30% reduction in unique on-GPU KV tensor memory for synthetic mixed-length conversational workload. 2) Median generation latency increase <= 3% compared to baseline for 95th percentile sequence lengths. 3) No incorrect generations introduced by reuse (validated with existing eval prompts). 4) Feature gated and rollout-able per-customer. 5) Comprehensive unit + integration tests and a monitoring dashboard that surfaces reuse rate and reference counts.
design_notes: High-level approach: 1) Normalize/Canonicalize prompt segments at token-level: strip non-essential whitespace, collapse repeated system metadata, and produce a stable token sequence. 2) Compute a compact content hash (64-bit + model/seqmeta salt) to identify candidate identical segments. 3) Shard the global prefix store by (model_variant, length_bucket, gpu_node) to avoid cross-GPU locking hot spots. 4) Store KV fragments as small on-device tensors plus a 64-bit reference ID; runtime maps request->fragment refs and assembles full KV view via indirection when dispatching to kernels. 5) Background consolidation: merge overlapping fragments into larger canonical fragments when contiguous reuse patterns appear to improve compute locality. 6) Eviction: LRU augmented by reuse_score (reuse_count / time_window) and estimated on-disk cost. 7) Safety: conservative matching only when canonicalization exact-match succeeds; optional fuzzy matching will be gated behind experiments.
implementation_steps: Spec canonicalization rules and unit tests (tokens -> canonical form)
Implement hash catalog and sharded in-memory index (prod-mode feature flag)
Modify request path to canonicalize prefixes for cache lookup before KV construction
Implement on-GPU reference indirection layer and reference-counted allocator
Add background consolidation worker and safe merge protocol
Add metrics: fragment_count, reuse_rate, avg_refs_per_fragment, on_gpu_kv_bytes
Run canary across dedicated capacity pool and compare against baseline traces
Roll out gradually with opt-out per customer and telemetry verification
risks_and_mitigation: Hash collisions: use 64-bit salted hash and confirm by exact canonical token comparison as secondary check
Increased CPU overhead during canonicalization: microbench canonicalizer and fallback path to skip canonicalization if CPU is saturated
Indirection cost: measure latency of indirection assembly; if high, perform eager materialization for hot fragments
Memory fragmentation on GPU: implement compaction pass during low-util windows
Correctness/regressions: keep strict feature flag and run eval-suite comparing outputs on diverse prompt sets
